events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 7 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The driver cancelled this RydeX trip as a rider no-show, but the GPS records show he was inside the 200 m pickup zone for only 2 min 50 s in total before cancelling (first entry 21:28:05, cancellation at 21:30:55), which is short of the required more-than-3-minutes wait. [F2 F5 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C2: The driver's stationary period at the pickup before cancellation lasted 2 min 5 s (21:28:50–21:30:55) at 39 m from the pickup point, so the 3:01 / 180-second waiting threshold in NS-1 is not met. [F3 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C3: Even counting from the earliest possible arrival marker (platform-recorded arrival 21:28:05, or the 'I'm Here' tap at 21:29:10), the driver cancelled just 2 min 50 s after arrival and 1 min 45 s after the tap — both under 3 minutes. [F5 F6] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: The driver's written statement claiming he 'waited at least 5 minutes' is contradicted by the system records and therefore cannot stand: acceptance was 21:26:00 and cancellation 21:30:55, and GPS shows only 2 min 50 s within the pickup zone. [F12 F4 F2] [NS-1 NS-2]
C5: Because the driver's no-show claim does not satisfy the waiting condition, the $6.61 cancellation fee charged on this trip must be refunded in full to the rider. [F8 F4] [NS-2 NS-7]
C6: The rider's own record is clean — 634-day-old account, rating 4.7, zero disputes and zero upheld complaints in 90 days — so there is no basis to treat this as rider abuse of the no-show process. [F16] [NS-2]
C7: The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days and 451 trips, i.e. this is a repeated pattern of premature no-show cancellations, supporting an account-review flag alongside the refund. [F17] [NS-2 NS-3]
Weaknesses: The driver did press the 'I'm Here' button and the chat shows he announced 'I'm here, silver Toyota Altis.' at 21:29 (F10), and his closest approach was 38 m (F1) — the other side will argue he genuinely was at the pickup and that the rider simply did not board in time. | The driver's statement says he waited 5 minutes (F12) and the timeline shows he tapped 'I'm Here' (F6); the other side will argue the wait should be counted from acceptance/arrival plus that he kept stationary at the curb, and that 2 min 50 s within 200 m is close enough to 3 minutes to be a measurement artefact rather than a policy breach. | The rider never appears in any message or record as responding to the driver's arrival ('I'm here' F10 went unanswered), so the driver will paint this as an uncontactable rider — though chats show the rider was charged a fee for a trip that never happened. | Timeline entries F6 and F7 conflict on whether the 'I'm Here' tap occurred; if the judge credits F7 (no tap), the NS-1 (i) element fails too, which still favours the rider but changes the reasoning.
Asks: refund_full $6.61

claims.assertion: The driver did reach the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m and he was inside 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 2 min 50 s before cancelling, having first entered that radius at 21:28:05.

The driver had a genuine presence at the pickup and no fraud indicator applies to him: there was no traffic or weather event forcing the cancellation, and the only disputed issue is the 3-minute wait threshold, not whether he showed up.

weaknesses: The 3-minute wait requirement in NS-1 (iii) is not met on the system record: cumulative time within 200 m is 2 min 50 s (F2) and the platform's recorded arrival-to-cancellation gap is 2 min 50 s (F5), i.e. under 3:01, so the rider's $6.61 was charged before the waiting threshold was reached.

The stationary stretch the driver relies on lasted 2 min 5 s at 39 m from the pickup (F3) before he cancelled at 21:30:55 (F4) — shorter still than the 3:01 threshold, so it confirms rather than cures the breach of NS-1(iii).

Notifying the rider is not a substitute for waiting: measured from the driver's own 21:29 'I'm here' message to his 21:30:55 cancellation, he gave the rider at most 1 min 55 s, and on F6's version only 1 min 45 s after the tap — both under 3 minutes, so NS-1(iii) still fails.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The driver cancelled this RydeX trip (F4), so NS-0 routes the $6.61 cancellation fee through NS-1/NS-2 rather than NS-3 [F4][NS-0]. The no-show fee is chargeable only if all three NS-1 elements hold: an "I'm Here" tap, GPS presence at the pickup at the time of the tap, and more than 3 minutes of waiting at the pickup thereafter [F6][NS-1].

NS-1(i) and (ii) are satisfied: the timeline records a tap at 21:29:10 with the driver 42 m from the pickup (F6), consistent with his closest approach of 38 m [F1][F6][NS-1]. NS-1(iii) fails on every measure. Cumulative time inside the 200 m radius before cancellation was 2 min 50 s (F2), the stationary spell ran only 21:28:50–21:30:55, i.e. 2 min 5 s (F3), and the platform's arrival-to-cancellation gap was likewise 2 min 50 s (F5) [F2][F3][F5][NS-1]. Even the most generous reading — measuring from the platform-recorded arrival — stays below the >180 s threshold [F5][NS-1].

The driver's written claim of a five-minute wait (F12) cannot cure this: acceptance was 21:26:00 and cancellation 21:30:55, only 4 min 55 s in total, and chat statements yield to the gps/timeline records [F4][F12][NS-1]. Since NS-1(iii) is unmet, NS-2 requires the $6.61 fee on record (F8) to be refunded in full, the amount being the recorded cancellation fee itself [F8][NS-2]. No fake-tap flag arises: the tap was made at 42 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m zone (F6, F1), so the NS-2 flag condition does not apply [F1][F6][NS-2].

The driver's profile — 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17) — is not relied on to decide the case, and the NS-2 flag_account consequence is not triggered because there is no fraudulent tap; profile facts may not decide a case and are not used here to escalate [F17][NS-2].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 rider cancellation fee as a Ryde voucher; record the driver's premature no-show cancellation against his no-show record; no account flag on this case.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled this RydeX trip as a rider no-show, but the GPS records show he was inside the 200 m pickup zone for only 2 min 50 s in total before cancelling (first entry 21:28:05, cancellation at 21:30:55), which is short of the required more-than-3-minutes wait.
The driver's stationary period at the pickup before cancellation lasted 2 min 5 s (21:28:50–21:30:55) at 39 m from the pickup point, so the 3:01 / 180-second waiting threshold in NS-1 is not met.

Even counting from the earliest possible arrival marker (platform-recorded arrival 21:28:05, or the 'I'm Here' tap at 21:29:10), the driver cancelled just 2 min 50 s after arrival and 1 min 45 s after the tap — both under 3 minutes.

The driver's written statement claiming he 'waited at least 5 minutes' is contradicted by the system records and therefore cannot stand: acceptance was 21:26:00 and cancellation 21:30:55, and GPS shows only 2 min 50 s within the pickup zone.
Because the driver's no-show claim does not satisfy the waiting condition, the $6.61 cancellation fee charged on this trip must be refunded in full to the rider.
The rider's own record is clean — 634-day-old account, rating 4.7, zero disputes and zero upheld complaints in 90 days — so there is no basis to treat this as rider abuse of the no-show process.
The driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days and 451 trips, i.e. this is a repeated pattern of premature no-show cancellations, supporting an account-review flag alongside the refund.

weaknesses: The driver did press the 'I'm Here' button and the chat shows he announced 'I'm here, silver Toyota Altis.' at 21:29 (F10), and his closest approach was 38 m (F1) — the other side will argue he genuinely was at the pickup and that the rider simply did not board in time.

The driver's statement says he waited 5 minutes (F12) and the timeline shows he tapped 'I'm Here' (F6); the other side will argue the wait should be counted from acceptance/arrival plus that he kept stationary at the curb, and that 2 min 50 s within 200 m is close enough to 3 minutes to be a measurement artefact rather than a policy breach.

The rider never appears in any message or record as responding to the driver's arrival ('I'm here' F10 went unanswered), so the driver will paint this as an uncontactable rider — though chats show the rider was charged a fee for a trip that never happened.
Timeline entries F6 and F7 conflict on whether the 'I'm Here' tap occurred; if the judge credits F7 (no tap), the NS-1 (i) element fails too, which still favours the rider but changes the reasoning.

claims.assertion: The driver did reach the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 38 m and he was inside 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 2 min 50 s before cancelling, having first entered that radius at 21:28:05.
The driver came to a halt and stayed at the pickup: he was stationary from 21:28:50 to 21:30:55 (2 min 5 s) at 39 m from the pickup point.
The rider was notified the driver had arrived — the driver messaged "I'm here, silver Toyota Altis" at 21:29 and only cancelled at 21:30:55, well after that message.
The driver's own account is that he waited at the pickup and the rider never came, and he cancelled as a no-show rather than for any other reason.
The fee in dispute is only the standard published rider cancellation fee of $6.61 with no surge, so no overcharge element exists on the fare record.

The driver had a genuine presence at the pickup and no fraud indicator applies to him: there was no traffic or weather event forcing the cancellation, and the only disputed issue is the 3-minute wait threshold, not whether he showed up.

weaknesses: The 3-minute wait requirement in NS-1 (iii) is not met on the system record: cumulative time within 200 m is 2 min 50 s (F2) and the platform's recorded arrival-to-cancellation gap is 2 min 50 s (F5), i.e. under 3:01, so the rider's $6.61 was charged before the waiting threshold was reached.

The timeline is internally inconsistent on whether the driver pressed "I'm Here": F6 says he tapped at 21:29:10 while 42 m away and waited only 1 min 45 s after the tap, but F7 says driver_pressed_here_at is null. On F6's version the post-tap wait is only 1 min 45 s, which also fails NS-1 (iii); on F7's version NS-1 (i) fails outright because the button was never pressed.

The driver's written statement that he "waited at least 5 minutes" (F12) is contradicted by the timeline showing he was only 4 min 55 s from acceptance (F4) and spent at most 2 min 50 s inside the pickup radius (F2), and chat statements lose to gps/timeline records.
The driver's profile already shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17), so the rider will argue this is a repeat pattern supporting NS-2's flag_account consequence rather than a one-off.

points.response: Conceded factually as to proximity, but it defeats the driver's case, not mine: being within 200 m for a cumulative 2 min 50 s (F2) is precisely what falls short of the NS-1(iii) requirement of more than 3 minutes inside the pickup zone, and the same 2 min 50 s is the platform-recorded arrival-to-cancellation gap (F5).

The stationary stretch the driver relies on lasted 2 min 5 s at 39 m from the pickup (F3) before he cancelled at 21:30:55 (F4) — shorter still than the 3:01 threshold, so it confirms rather than cures the breach of NS-1(iii).

Notifying the rider is not a substitute for waiting: measured from the driver's own 21:29 'I'm here' message to his 21:30:55 cancellation, he gave the rider at most 1 min 55 s, and on F6's version only 1 min 45 s after the tap — both under 3 minutes, so NS-1(iii) still fails.

The driver's no-show claim rests on his written statement that he 'waited at least 5 minutes' (F12), but that is impossible on the system record: acceptance was 21:26:00 and cancellation 21:30:55, only 4 min 55 s total (F4), with at most 2 min 50 s inside the pickup radius (F2), so the statement loses under the system-records-first rule.

The amount being the standard published figure (F8, F9, no surge) is irrelevant: NS-0 makes the $6.61 chargeable only if NS-1 is satisfied, and here it is not, so the correct outcome is refund_full under NS-2, not no_action.

I do not allege the driver never showed up — I allege he charged a cancellation fee before completing the mandatory 3-minute wait, which is exactly what F2 (2 min 50 s within 200 m) and F5 (2 min 50 s arrival-to-cancel gap) prove; the absence of traffic or weather events (F13, F14, F15) gives him no independent justification for cancelling early.

My claim stands on the two independent system measures — 2 min 50 s cumulative within 200 m (F2) and the platform's own 2 min 50 s arrival-to-cancellation gap (F5) — and the driver's brief itself concedes the 3-minute threshold is unmet.

Given the two upheld no-show disputes on the driver's record in 90 days (F17), I maintain the rider's clean profile (F16) and ask the panel to record the refund and additionally refer the driver's account for review under NS-2/NS-6-style repeated-premature-cancellation scrutiny.

Conceded on the arithmetic: on the system record the driver was inside the 200 m zone for a cumulative 2 min 50 s before cancelling (F2, F5), which falls short of the >180 s threshold in NS-1 (iii), so the no-show cancellation fee is not made out under NS-1.
Conceded: the stationary spell at the pickup ran 21:28:50–21:30:55, i.e. 2 min 5 s at 39 m (F3), so NS-1 (iii) is not satisfied on any reading of the stationary period.

Conceded: whether measured from platform-recorded arrival at 21:28:05 (2 min 50 s) or from the 'I'm Here' tap at 21:29:10 (1 min 45 s), both intervals are under 3 minutes (F5, F6), so NS-1 (iii) fails.

Conceded: the driver's written claim of a five-minute wait (F12) is contradicted by the timeline (acceptance 21:26:00, cancellation 21:30:55) and by the 2 min 50 s inside the pickup zone (F4, F2), and chat statements lose to system records.
Conceded: because NS-1 is not satisfied, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee on record (F8) to be refunded in full and the trip should not be charged.

Not contested as a fact, but it is irrelevant to the only element that decides this case: the rider's clean history (F16) cannot supply the >180 s wait that NS-1 (iii) requires, nor can it override the 2 min 50 s shown by GPS (F2).

The profile history (F17) may at most support an additional flag_account action under RD-6/NS-7 style account review, but profile facts can never decide the case and I thus accept the refund while the reason for it is the shortfall under NS-1 (F2, F5), not any routing or fraud finding.
